subject: Insurance
title: Building Codes Born from Loss
description: A micro-lesson that makes Building Codes Born from Loss usable.

hook.text: Every major building code in history was written after a disaster insurance paid for. Safety rules are born from claims.

buildup.text: After each great fire, insurers demanded changes: brick walls, fire exits, sprinkler systems. Pay once, prevent twice.

discovery.text: The National Fire Protection Association, founded in 1896.

twist.text: Insurers became the invisible regulators of safety.

climax.text: Insurance doesn't just pay for disasters—it prevents them.

punchline.text: Insurers wrote the safety rules. Every building code started with a claim.

quiz.question: Who primarily backed the National Fire Protection Association?
